prompt: Run this complete script fresh. RETRYABLE lists the statuses that are worth retrying. What is printed?

options.text: attempt 1 failed with 503 / attempt 2 failed with 404 / ok 3. Every error is retried, so the third call succeeds and its ok is returned.
options.feedback: Only statuses in RETRYABLE are retried. 404 is not in the set, so the function returns stopped at that point.

options.text: attempt 1 failed with 503 / stopped 1. The first failure ends the loop, because a 503 is a server error that is not retried.
options.feedback: 503 is in RETRYABLE, so the loop goes on to the second call. It stops only for the 404.

options.text: attempt 1 failed with 503 / attempt 2 failed with 404 / gave up 2. After the 404 the loop still ends with gave up, since it simply runs out.
options.feedback: A non-retryable status makes the function return stopped at once, so the final return gave up is not reached.

options.text: attempt 1 failed with 503 / attempt 2 failed with 404 / stopped 2. Every 4xx error is the caller's fault and can never succeed on retry.
options.feedback: The output is right, but the rule is wrong: some 4xx statuses, such as 429 (too many requests) or 408 (request timeout), are routinely retried. The code stops because 404 is not in RETRYABLE, not because of its class.
options.partial_reason: Correct: the printed lines and the stop at 404. Incorrect: that every 4xx is permanent; the set decides, and some 4xx statuses are retried.

options.text: attempt 1 failed with 503 / attempt 2 failed with 404 / stopped 2. 503 is retried, 404 is not in RETRYABLE, so it stops after 2 calls.
options.feedback: Correct. The first failure is a 503, which is in the set, so there is a second call. That fails with a 404, which is not in the set, so the function returns stopped. Two calls were made and the ok is never reached.

explanation: Call 1 fails with 503, which is printed. 503 is in RETRYABLE, so the loop continues. Call 2 fails with 404, which is printed; 404 is not in RETRYABLE, so fetch returns stopped. client.calls is 2. The ok at the end of the script is never reached. A permanent error such as 404 would fail the same way on every retry, so retrying it only adds load.

expected.stdout:
attempt 1 failed with 503
attempt 2 failed with 404
stopped 2

verification.rationale: The displayed script produces the expected output deterministically (integer simulated time, visible failure script). A matching output alone cannot separate the correct model from the half-credit model, so that reasoning needs human review.
verification.limitations: Simulated only: scripted FakeClient failures and, where time matters, an integer-ms Clock; no real time, I/O, randomness or imports (contract R1-R4). The misconception models are uncalibrated editorial hypotheses, not prevalence claims. A simulation shows the stated model, not a real network.
